correctness.rationale: The exact identity \(\tau(\tau(ab))=(\omega(a)+u_b+1)\tau(v_b)\) holds for the unique coprime squarefree/powerful decomposition. The fourth-moment estimate is proved by centered prime-indicator expansion with cutoff \(Y=y^{1/10}\): the floor-function discrepancy is \(O(Y^4/y)\), and the independent Bernoulli fourth moment is \(O((\log\log y)^2)\). This yields at most \(O(y/(\log\log y)^2)\) exceptional integers, negligible after reciprocal normalization. Mobius inclusion-exclusion supplies the fixed-powerful-part squarefree density. The remaining powerful part is bounded, uniformly after normalization, by \(O(B^{-1/2})+o(1)\), by splitting at \(b=\sqrt x\) and using the powerful-integer count \(O(\sqrt t)\). This justifies passage to the positive convergent constant series. The checker confirms the finite arithmetic identities at all \(200000\) integers in its stated domain.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 paper names precisely the stronger asymptotic with a positive constant as Conjecture (8), after proving only comparability. This result resolves that natural central quantitative gap, identifies the constant through a convergent series over canonical powerful parts, and provides a reusable analytic device distinguishing main-term from exceptional-set mass. It is not a routine restatement of the published order of magnitude.
